name: Flashlight Phonics Cave
mechanic: A dark cave wall hides many picture-objects in shadow. The child is told a target sound (e.g. /b/) and drags a flashlight beam across the wall; the beam softly illuminates whatever it passes over, but only objects whose NAME BEGINS with the target sound 'wake up' (glow, wiggle, smile) when lit. The child taps the glowing ones to collect them into a jar.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is i-spy-scene (find named items in a scene) and pop-the-right-ones. Separation: the items are HIDDEN in darkness and only the moving beam reveals them — discovery is spatial+continuous (sweep to expose) rather than a static scan, and the phonetic match is the gate for the reveal-glow itself, not just for scoring. The flashlight-as-reveal-tool is the core, not the tap.
fun_no_competition: Suspenseful sweep-and-discover in the dark; the delight of an object 'waking up' and glowing when your beam finds it; filling a glowing jar of collected sound-friends.
character_world: A friendly cave-bat guide named Echo who lives in the Sound Cave and cheers when you wake a sleeping object.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — beam = a radial-gradient mask div following pointer; objects are absolutely-positioned sprites with opacity tied to beam proximity (CSS + a tiny pointermove handler), glow = CSS class toggled when name-onset matches.
asset_idea: Stub: gray cave-wall bg + 8-10 grayscale object silhouettes + a cone-of-light PNG + glow halo. CA5 art: painted rock cave with cracks, Echo the bat, warm flashlight cone, per-object 'awake' (smiling) and 'asleep' (dim) frames.

name: X-Ray Number Bones
mechanic: A vet's x-ray table holds a stuffed animal; the child slides an x-ray scanner panel over it to reveal a hidden cluster of dots/bones inside. They must look at the revealed quantity and tap the numeral (or ten-frame) that matches how many they see — the dots stay revealed only while the scanner hovers, so they subitize/count under the lens.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is reveal-grid (uncover a hidden picture). Separation: nothing is being collected or completed; the reveal is a temporary x-ray window the child controls, and the SKILL is reading the hidden quantity exposed inside a body — a counting/cardinality act, not a picture-completion act. The hover-to-reveal-then-it-hides forces real looking.
fun_no_competition: The novelty of x-ray vision; the gentle reveal of glowing bones inside a cuddly creature; satisfying 'ding' as the right number lights up and the animal gets a sticker bandage.
character_world: Dr. Pip, a kindly toy-vet whose patients are plush animals that need a count of their tummy-dots.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — scanner is a draggable div with a clip/mask revealing a second 'inner' image layer; numeral choices are tappable tiles. No game loop; pure DOM masking.
asset_idea: Stub: plush-animal outline + an inner dot-cluster layer + a translucent blue scanner rectangle + numeral tiles. CA5: warm vet-clinic, plush patients with cute faces, glowing x-ray skeleton/dot innards, Dr. Pip in a tiny coat.

name: Footprint Detective
mechanic: An animal walked across snow/mud leaving a TRAIL of clue tracks plus other evidence (a tuft of fur, a dropped acorn, a feather). The child follows/taps the trail of footprints in order to 'gather clues', and at the end deduces which of 3-4 suspect animals made them by matching attributes (this print has 4 toes + the fur is orange → the fox). They tap the deduced culprit.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is path-journey (move along a path) and match-pairs. Separation: the path here is a CLUE-GATHERING deduction trail, not a route to traverse for its own sake; the answer is DEDUCED by narrowing suspects from accumulated evidence, a logical-attribute reasoning act. No two clues alone solve it — the discovery is inferential.
fun_no_competition: Playing detective; the 'aha' of clues adding up; a magnifying-glass cursor that enlarges each clue with a satisfying pop; the reveal of the culprit peeking out from behind a bush, caught (gently, smiling).
character_world: Detective Mittens, a cat in a deerstalker hat with a magnifying glass, on the Case of the Missing Cookie.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — clues are tappable hotspots that flip open a fact card; suspects are 3-4 sprites; deduction = match accumulated attribute flags. Logic is simple state, no loop. Authoring the attribute sets is the real work.
asset_idea: Stub: snowy scene + footprint trail + 3 clue icons + 4 suspect animal cards. CA5: storybook woodland mystery scene, Detective Mittens, glowing magnifier, animated 'caught!' reveal of the culprit.

name: Fog-Lift Word Mountain
mechanic: A target sight-word (or CVC word) sits behind thick fog. The child taps the matching picture/letter-sound choices one at a time; each CORRECT tap blows away one patch of fog, progressively REVEALING the hidden word underneath until it's fully readable — at which point the child reads it aloud (Hear-it confirms). Wrong taps puff a tiny harmless cloud, no penalty.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is reveal-grid (correct answers uncover a picture tile-by-tile). Separation: what's revealed is a WORD being spelled into legibility, and the reveal is CONTINUOUS fog dissipation rather than discrete grid tiles, tied to letter-sound or sight-word matching. The discovery payoff is reading the word that emerges, an ELA act not a picture-puzzle.
fun_no_competition: Atmospheric suspense of fog lifting; the dreamy reveal of a mountaintop word; wind 'whoosh' sound and a sunrise breaking through when the word is fully clear.
character_world: Nimbus, a little cloud-sheep who lives on Word Mountain and clears the sky for you.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — fog = overlay div with multiple semi-opaque patches removed on each correct answer (opacity/transform transitions); word text beneath revealed by removing patches. No loop.
asset_idea: Stub: mountain bg + word text layer + 5-6 fog-patch PNGs + choice tiles. CA5: misty pastel mountain, Nimbus the cloud-sheep, layered drifting fog, golden sunrise reveal frame.

name: What's Behind the Door (Deduce)
mechanic: Three closed doors each hide an animal/object; a row of YES/NO clue lights gives attribute hints ('It is BIG: yes', 'It has WINGS: no', 'It is RED: yes'). The child uses the clues to eliminate doors and predicts which single door holds the matching thing, then taps that door to open it and confirm. Clues are revealed one at a time so deduction tightens.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is sort-home and match-pairs. Separation: the answer is HIDDEN behind doors and reached by ELIMINATION from attribute clues (process-of-elimination logic), not by sorting or pairing visible items. The reveal is the suspenseful door-open that confirms a deduction already made.
fun_no_competition: Game-show 'pick a door' suspense without competition; clue-lights flicking on; the door creaking open to reveal the friend, who waves; you were right because you thought it through.
character_world: Hosty, a cheerful curtain-tassel character on the Discovery Doors stage.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — doors = clickable divs with an open-state sprite swap; clue lights = sequential reveal of attribute booleans; logic = attribute matching across 3 candidates. Trivial state.
asset_idea: Stub: 3 door panels + clue-light row + hidden-item sprites. CA5: playful stage with curtains, ornate doors, Hosty tassel, doors swinging open with a sparkle and the revealed character waving.

name: Magnifier Spelling Bug Hunt
mechanic: A leaf is covered in tiny camouflaged bugs, each bug carrying ONE letter on its back. The child is given a target word and drags a big magnifying lens over the leaf; only under the lens do the small letters become big and readable. They must find and tap the bug-letters IN ORDER to spell the word, the lens being the only way to read what each bug holds.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is i-spy-scene and magic-trace. Separation: the letters are too small to read until MAGNIFIED — the lens is a true reveal tool that changes legibility, and the task is ordered spelling (sequence) gated by a search-and-magnify discovery, not free scanning or tracing.
fun_no_competition: Delight of zooming in to read a hidden letter; bugs that wiggle when magnified; the word filling in bug-by-bug at the bottom; a happy buzz when the word is complete.
character_world: Lupe the ladybug, a tiny entomologist who hands you her magnifier.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — lens = draggable div with a CSS scale transform on a clipped region (or per-bug scale-up when under lens via proximity check); ordered-tap spelling = simple sequence state.
asset_idea: Stub: leaf bg + scattered small bug sprites with letters + magnifier graphic. CA5: lush macro leaf world, charming letter-bugs, glass-lens distortion ring, Lupe with a tiny notebook.

name: Develop the Photo (Counting Darkroom)
mechanic: A blank photo print sits in developer fluid. The child gently 'rocks/swishes' the tray (drag back-and-forth), and with each swish the photo DEVELOPS more, slowly revealing a scene full of objects. Once developed, they answer 'how many [ducks] are in the photo?' by counting the now-visible items and tapping the number — the developing IS the reveal of the things to count.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is reveal-grid and i-spy-scene. Separation: the reveal is a tactile DEVELOPING process (swish to bring the latent image up) under the child's pacing, and the math act counts items that only EXIST once developed. The darkroom develop-the-latent-image metaphor is the unique core, distinct from sweeping a beam or lifting fog.
fun_no_competition: The magic of a photo appearing from nothing; the sloshy swish sound; surprise at what scene develops; counting your developed snapshot and pinning it on a clothesline gallery.
character_world: Flicker the firefly photographer in a cozy red-lit darkroom.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — develop = increasing opacity/contrast filter on the photo layer driven by swish count (pointermove distance accumulator); counting = tap a numeral. CSS filter transitions, no loop.
asset_idea: Stub: developer tray + blank-to-scene photo layer + numeral tiles + clothesline. CA5: red-lit darkroom, Flicker firefly, photo emerging with grain/contrast, clothesline gallery of developed counts.

name: Sound Sonar (Hidden in the Deep)
mechanic: Sea creatures hide in dark water. The child taps a sonar 'ping' button which sends a ripple; hidden creatures briefly flash their silhouette AND a sound plays (the spoken NAME of the creature, or its initial sound). The child must, by the audio cue + silhouette, identify and tap where the named-target creature is hiding before the ping fades — using sense/detection rather than sight.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is pop-the-right-ones and i-spy-scene. Separation: the things are INVISIBLE until pinged and the primary detection channel is AUDIO/echo (sense what you can't see), pairing a heard name/sound to a momentarily-revealed location — a listening+phoneme task driven by active sensing, not visual scanning.
fun_no_competition: Submarine sonar suspense; the ping ripple and creature-flash; pairing a sound you hear to a shape you glimpse; gentle bubbles and a friendly creature surfacing to say hello when found.
character_world: Captain Dot, a small submarine-driving otter exploring the Quiet Deep.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — ping = an expanding circle animation that briefly toggles opacity on hidden sprites + triggers an audio cue (LCSAudio); tap-to-find = hotspot check. Brief CSS-timed reveal, no loop.
asset_idea: Stub: dark-water bg + hidden creature silhouettes + sonar button + sub. CA5: deep-sea blues, glowing sonar ripple, charming sea creatures (silhouette + lit forms), Captain Dot's porthole sub.

name: Lift-the-Flap Math Story
mechanic: A story scene shows e.g. '3 bunnies are visiting. Some are hiding under the bushes!' Several bushes/boxes are closed flaps. The child is told the WHOLE (5 bunnies total) and sees some (3 in the open); they tap flaps to peek under each, revealing how many are hidden, and must decide the missing PART (how many are hidden = 2) by tapping the numeral — combining seen + hidden to make the whole.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is reveal-grid and feed-the-friend. Separation: this is part-part-whole DECOMPOSITION driven by lifting flaps to discover the hidden addend — the reveal directly serves the math (hidden quantity = the unknown part). Discovery answers an addition/decomposition question, not a picture or a counting-only task.
fun_no_competition: Lift-the-flap surprise (classic board-book joy); the giggle of bunnies peeking out; figuring out the hidden number; flaps that bounce open with a soft pop.
character_world: Burrow the bunny family in a meadow full of hiding spots.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — flaps = clickable divs with an open-state showing the hidden count; whole/part logic = simple arithmetic check; numeral choices tappable. No loop.
asset_idea: Stub: meadow + bushes/boxes as flaps + bunny sprites + numeral tiles. CA5: storybook meadow, lift-flap bushes with shadow underneath, peeking bunnies, soft pop-open animation.

name: Color-Filter Lens Reveal
mechanic: A page looks like meaningless colored noise/scribble. The child drags one of several colored filter lenses (red/blue/green) over it; ONLY the correct filter makes a hidden picture or word pop out of the camouflage (like a red-lens decoder). The task: read the prompt ('find the lens that reveals a CAT'), try lenses, and tap the picture once revealed — choosing the right tool to expose hidden info.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is reveal-grid and sort-home. Separation: the reveal requires picking the RIGHT decoder tool (color filter) — a tool-selection-to-expose mechanic with secret-decoder delight; nothing is being completed or sorted. Distinct from the flashlight (continuous sweep) and x-ray (window) because here the discovery is choosing which lens unlocks the image.
fun_no_competition: Secret-decoder-ring magic; the thrill when the right filter makes a hidden picture leap out of chaos; swapping lenses to see what each reveals; collecting decoded secrets in a spy notebook.
character_world: Agent Acorn, a squirrel spy with a satchel of decoder lenses.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — filter = a tinted overlay + a hidden layer that becomes visible only under a matching CSS mix-blend/mask; lens drag swaps which hidden layer shows. CSS blend modes + masks; no loop.
asset_idea: Stub: noise bg + per-color hidden image layers + 3 colored lens PNGs + spy notebook. CA5: spy-lab aesthetic, Agent Acorn, glossy decoder lenses, camouflage patterns that resolve into clean pictures.

name: Dust-for-Prints Letter Match
mechanic: An invisible fingerprint sits on a surface. The child 'dusts' (drag a brush back-and-forth) to gradually reveal a hidden UPPERCASE letter print. Once revealed, a line-up of lowercase 'suspects' appears and the child taps the lowercase letter that MATCHES the dusted uppercase print (case-matching) — the forensic dusting reveals the clue to be matched.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is match-pairs and magic-trace. Separation: the thing-to-match is HIDDEN and must be uncovered by a brushing/dusting reveal gesture before matching is even possible; the forensic dust-for-prints metaphor and the upper/lower case-matching standard are distinct from any pair-flip or trace.
fun_no_competition: CSI-for-kids fun of dusting a hidden print into view; brush-swish particles; the reveal of a glowing letter; matching it to its little partner and clipping the case to a board.
character_world: Officer Whiskers, a forensic cat at the Letter Lab.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — dust reveal = brush drag accumulates over a masked canvas region exposing the letter (canvas alpha-clear or per-region opacity); match = tap lowercase tile. Canvas brushing is a known simple pattern.
asset_idea: Stub: surface bg + hidden uppercase-letter mask + lowercase tiles + brush. CA5: forensic lab desk, Officer Whiskers, glowing dusted prints, fingerprint-dust particles, evidence clipboard.

name: Treasure Map Clue Trail (Sequence)
mechanic: A treasure map shows a start and several numbered/lettered stepping spots, but the route is hidden. The child reveals the path by following ordered CLUES: 'first the spot that starts with /m/', 'next the spot that comes after 2', etc. Each correct choice uncovers the next leg of the trail (a dotted line + footprint) until the whole route to the treasure is revealed and the chest opens.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is path-journey. Separation: in path-journey you traverse a KNOWN path; here the path is HIDDEN and you DISCOVER/construct it by solving an ordered clue at each step (sequence + letter/number recognition). The reveal is the route itself emerging from correct deductions, not movement along a given track.
fun_no_competition: Pirate-treasure-map adventure; each clue uncovering a new dotted leg with a stamp of a footprint; the X-marks-the-spot chest bursting open with confetti at the end.
character_world: Pip the parrot navigator and a friendly map that draws itself.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — clue sequence = ordered state; each correct tap reveals a path-segment (SVG line draw or sprite). Logic is straightforward sequence checking; no loop.
asset_idea: Stub: parchment map + spot markers + dotted-line segments + chest. CA5: aged treasure map, Pip parrot, footprint stamps, animated dotted trail drawing in, treasure chest open frame.

name: Peek-a-Boo Rhyme Curtain
mechanic: A puppet-theater curtain is mostly closed; behind it a picture peeks through a narrow gap. The child hears/sees a target word and must pick, from a row of word-pictures, the one that RHYMES. Each correct rhyme pick parts the curtain a little more, revealing more of the hidden surprise puppet behind it; the full reveal (a costumed character taking a bow) comes when the rhyme set is complete.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is fog-lift (04) and reveal-grid. Separation: the reveal is a CURTAIN PARTING (horizontal theatrical open) gated specifically by RHYME recognition (phonological), and the payoff is a character reveal/bow rather than reading a word. The theater-curtain peek and rhyme gate distinguish it from fog (atmospheric, letter-sound) and grid (tiles, pictures).
fun_no_competition: Puppet-show suspense; the wiggling peek of something behind the curtain; the joy of the curtain opening wider with each rhyme; the surprise character taking a bow at full reveal.
character_world: The Rhyme Theater, hosted by a velvet-curtain spirit and a mystery guest puppet each round.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — curtain = two panel divs that translate apart in steps on each correct rhyme; choices tappable; rhyme matching = data-driven. CSS transforms, no loop.
asset_idea: Stub: theater frame + 2 curtain panels + hidden puppet + rhyme-picture tiles. CA5: ornate puppet theater, velvet curtains, spotlight, surprise puppets (peek + full bow frames).

name: Heat-Sense Hidden Animals
mechanic: Animals are camouflaged invisibly in a habitat. The child drags a thermal/heat-sensor scope; under it the scene shows in heat-vision and warm-blooded animals glow as colored heat-blobs (while rocks/plants stay cool). They must use the heat-glow to FIND a target animal and count how many warm creatures are hiding — sensing temperature to detect the hidden living things.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is flashlight (01) and x-ray (02). Separation: the detection channel is HEAT/temperature (a different sense), revealing only LIVING/warm things as glowing blobs amid cool decoys — a sense-the-hidden-property mechanic. The thermal-vision shift (whole-scene recolor under the scope) and living-vs-nonliving discrimination set it apart.
fun_no_competition: Wildlife-tracker thermal-goggles cool-factor; the scene recoloring into glowing heat under the scope; spotting a hidden critter by its warmth and counting the warm friends; a gentle 'found you!' as each surfaces.
character_world: Ranger Fern and her thermal goggles on a nighttime safari.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — scope = draggable div clipping a second 'thermal' version of the scene (recolored layer); warm animals = sprites visible only in thermal layer; count = tap numeral. DOM masking, no loop.
asset_idea: Stub: habitat bg (normal) + thermal-recolored bg + hidden warm-animal blobs + scope. CA5: night habitat, Ranger Fern, thermal-palette (blue→red) version, glowing animal heat-signatures, goggle frame.

name: Scratch-Off Secret Word
mechanic: A silver scratch-off panel hides a picture or word. The child scratches (drag) to reveal it, but the panel only lets them scratch ONE small window — so they must guess from the partial reveal. After a peek, a set of word/picture choices appears and the child taps which word matches the partially-revealed image (or which beginning sound it has) — deduction from incomplete reveal.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is develop-photo (07) and dust-for-prints (11). Separation: the reveal is DELIBERATELY PARTIAL (a single scratched window) forcing a GUESS from incomplete information, then confirming — an inference-from-fragment skill. Distinct from full developing/dusting (which fully reveal) by withholding the rest until the guess is made.
fun_no_competition: Lottery-ticket scratch-off thrill (without stakes); the gritty scratch sound and silver shavings; guessing from a sliver; the satisfying full-reveal confirmation when you guessed right.
character_world: Sketch the raccoon at the Surprise Stand handing out mystery scratch cards.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — scratch = canvas alpha-clearing over a small allowed region (clip to the window); choices tappable; partial-image inference is just authoring. Canvas scratch is a standard recipe.
asset_idea: Stub: silver panel + hidden picture + scratch window mask + choice tiles. CA5: carnival surprise-stand, Sketch raccoon, silver foil with shavings, a peek-window framing, reveal sparkle.

name: Weigh the Mystery Boxes
mechanic: Several wrapped boxes hide objects; the child can't see inside but CAN drop each box onto a balance scale to sense its weight (heavy boxes sink the pan, light ones rise). Given a clue ('the present is the HEAVIEST one' or 'the one that weighs the SAME as two blocks'), they compare weights by balancing and deduce which hidden box matches, then open it.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is sort-home and match-pairs. Separation: the hidden property is WEIGHT, sensed via a balance (compare-by-feel, not sight), and the answer is DEDUCED by ordering/comparing the unseen — a measurement-comparison detection. The 'sense weight of hidden things' core is unlike any visual or audio reveal here.
fun_no_competition: Mystery-box suspense; the see-saw tilt of the balance as a heavy box thunks down; deducing by weight and unwrapping to see if your hunch was right; ribbon bursting off the box.
character_world: Tilly the tapir at the Weigh Station with her wobbly balance scale.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — drag box onto a pan → CSS tilt the balance based on a stored weight value; compare states = simple numeric logic; open = sprite swap. Animation is transform-based, no physics loop.
asset_idea: Stub: balance scale + wrapped boxes (with weight data) + reveal contents. CA5: cozy weigh-station, Tilly tapir, tilting brass balance, wrapped presents, ribbon-burst open frames.

name: Decoder Wheel Secret Message
mechanic: A short message is shown in symbol-code; a hidden letter sits behind each symbol. The child turns a decoder wheel (drag-rotate) to line a symbol up with the alphabet ring, REVEALING which letter it stands for, then taps that letter to fill the message slot. Decoding symbol→letter across the word spells a real word that, once cracked, plays/animates (e.g. 'CAT' → a cat appears).
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is color-filter (10) and magic-machine. Separation: the reveal is achieved by ROTATING a decoder wheel to map a symbol to its hidden letter — a cipher-cracking, letter-correspondence act (print/letter-sound) rather than picking a filter. The rotary decode-each-symbol-then-spell flow is its own core.
fun_no_competition: Secret-agent cipher cracking; the click of the wheel turning and a symbol's letter snapping into view; cracking the whole message and watching it come to life; collecting decoded words in a codebook.
character_world: Cipher the fox, a junior codebreaker with a brass decoder wheel.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — wheel = a rotatable div (transform rotate on drag, snap to letter positions); symbol→letter lookup reveals on alignment; tap to place. Rotation + snap is simple; no loop.
asset_idea: Stub: decoder wheel (2 rings) + symbol message + letter slots + reveal animation. CA5: spy-desk, Cipher fox, ornate brass code wheel, glowing symbol-to-letter reveals, codebook.

name: Riddle Reveal (Narrow It Down)
mechanic: A hidden mystery picture is behind a small peephole; a riddle gives clues one line at a time ('I am yellow. I am a fruit. Monkeys love me.'). After each clue the child can ELIMINATE candidates from a small gallery and may take an early guess by tapping a candidate; guessing right opens the peephole fully to reveal the answer celebrating. Fewer clues needed = more of the surprise stays a surprise.
why_distinct: Closest neighbor is door-deduce (05) and footprint-detective (03). Separation: this is a RIDDLE-based progressive narrowing tied to ELA vocabulary/attribute language (listening to descriptive clues and matching meaning), with an open-ended 'guess whenever ready' that keeps suspense — distinct from binary yes/no doors (05, math classify) and physical footprint forensics (03, story details).
fun_no_competition: Classic riddle 'I spy with descriptive clues' delight; the peephole teasing a glimpse; the suspense of guessing early or waiting; the answer popping out and high-fiving you.
character_world: Riddle the owl, keeper of the Peephole of Puzzles.
web_shell_feasibility: feasible — clue reveal = sequential text; gallery candidates tappable with eliminate (dim) state; peephole reveal = mask expand on correct. Authoring riddle/attribute sets is the work; runtime is simple.
asset_idea: Stub: peephole frame + hidden answer + clue text + candidate gallery. CA5: cozy riddle-room, Riddle the owl, brass peephole, dim-out eliminated cards, answer-character celebration.
